commits.subject: privacy: implement threat-model recommendations TM1-TM15
commits.message:
privacy: implement threat-model recommendations TM1-TM15

Reduce what RPC providers, relayers, website hosts and on-chain
observers learn about a seller, following the prioritized list in
docs/threat-model/PRIVACY_THREAT_MODEL.md section 9. This is a
testnet-only, pre-audit change; it does not make payments anonymous.

Web app
- TM1: Sweep reads the one-time address balance only on an explicit
  "Check balance" click, for all users.
- TM2: per-flow provider-exposure notices for Scan, BTC, Solana and TRON.
- TM4: RPC URLs with key-like path or query secrets are flagged; a
  session-only option keeps them out of localStorage.
- TM5: apply-csp postbuild step; GHOSTPAY_CONNECT_ORIGINS narrows
  connect-src in _headers and the meta CSP (opt-in, documented).
- TM7: non-blocking warning when a sweep destination was already used
  in this browser (local record only).
- TM8: checkpoint slots are HMAC-keyed with the viewing key (v3),
  migrated from the v2 sha256 slots without losing checkpoints.
- TM9: receipts omit the one-time address unless the seller opts in;
  old receipts still verify.
- TM10: invoices are encrypted by default; passphrase and opt-out kept.
- TM12: opt-in bulk receipt evidence (bulkEvidence, default off).
- TM13: BTC spends detected from scanned blocks, with a sign-time check
  against the server; Solana and TRON balances read only at review.
- TM14: Tor Browser and own-node profile selection behind a first-use
  notice; defaults unchanged; Tor and own-node marked UNVERIFIED.
- TM15: padded scan windows (padBlocks, default 0).

Libraries
- chain-adapters: fetch sends credentials omit, no-referrer and
  no-store (TM3); bulk evidence fetch helpers (TM12).
- invoice-schema: stealthAddress optional in receipts (TM9).
- scan-source: padRange/fetchPadded (TM15); PIR behind experimental
  flag, default off.
- net-transport: profile selection (TM14).

Relayer
- TM11: optional request padding (pad field), ingress modes, zero-log
  switch; quote-tuple change assessed and not made (see PRIVACY.md).

Docs: threat model, sweep privacy, Tor, BUILD-WEB, relayer PRIVACY.

Verification: build:libs, web production build with postbuild CSP and
bundle scan, web tests (2795 passed), chain-adapters, invoice-schema,
scan-source, net-transport and relayer tests, lint, i18n check and
secret/action-pinning scans all exit 0. Not verified against real Tor,
OHTTP, own-node or public RPC networks.

Attest the Pages artifact checksums before deploying

SEC-43: the served files' SHA256SUMS existed only in the run summary and
a 14-day artifact, unsigned, so nothing durable bound the published site
to this repository's workflow. A new attest job (publishing runs only,
needs site, acceptance and release-gates; deploy now needs it) downloads

the Pages artifact), checks that SHA256SUMS lists exactly the served
files with well-formed lines and that every hash matches, then runs
actions/attest-build-provenance with subject-checksums. Pinned to
4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2 (resolved with
`git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/actions/attest-build-provenance`:
v4.2.2 and v4^{} both point there; release.yml already pins the same).
The job holds only id-token: write and attestations: write, with no
checkout and no repository code. Signing the sums with the release key
stays owner-gated (OD-07); SRI is not applicable to a same-origin static
bundle under the meta CSP and is not added here.

commits.subject: Add the spec 18 stealth key export codec (K01, K02, K05, K06)
commits.message:
Add the spec 18 stealth key export codec (K01, K02, K05, K06)

New framework-independent codec in @ghostpay/ux-vault/portable
(createStealthExportApi, same injection pattern as createKeystoreApi):
- ghostpay-stealth-public-v1: strict parser (bounds before parse, ASCII
  only, strict JSON, exact key sets, EIP-55 equality, curve points,
  public key to address binding) and serializer.
- buildVerifiedPayment: scheme 1 and chain checks, deriveStealthSecret
  with ignoreViewTag (deep-scan payments are eligible), address
  recomputed independently with addressOfSecret, key wiped on failure.
- ghostpay-stealth-keypair-v1 (single, selected, all-discovered; at most
  1024; export-time dedupe and conflict rules; address order) and
  ghostpay-stealth-master-v1: scrypt plus non-extractable AES-256-GCM,
  AAD = domain + canonical header, KDF bounds checked before the KDF,
  keystore passphrase policy, atomic import that wipes everything.
- formatRawPrivateKey (section 6 text) and detectStealthExportFormat.

Bodies are encoded and decoded as fixed canonical bytes, so no secret
becomes a JS string except in the deliberate raw-key text.

Independent vectors (node:crypto, noble, viem; no @ghostpay import) from
the scheme1-001 test keys, with byte-exact encrypt/decrypt tests and a
fast-check mutation suite. The error.stealthExport.* keys are added to
all four catalogs and classified as security keys.

Format doc fixes (gaps found while implementing): dedupe tie-break so
the output does not depend on input order; importers require exactly
canonical plaintext, so the ciphertext length is fixed and checked
before the KDF; blockNumber at most 2^64-1; exporter key order and no
trailing newline; raw key text uses LF with a final LF; public-only
records are not authenticated.

Add the spec 18 web export, re-authentication and recovery UI (K03-K06)

Web binding lib/stealthExport.ts over the shared codec, and lib/paymentKeyExport.ts
orchestration: public record, single encrypted keypair, gated raw key, encrypted
all-discovered archive (deduplicated per formats section 4), master backup and
recovery of any ghostpay-stealth-* file in a fresh session.

Re-authentication (resolves the open K03 decision): keyVault
requireSecretExportAuthorization takes the vault passphrase or a keystore backup
file of exactly the loaded keys and always returns a guard; with no vault the
export is refused. It records nothing (new session.ts helper
verifyCredentialForCurrentSession; no backup verification side effect).

Every secret export captures a session guard and the panel's operation signal,
checks them after every await and before returning text, checks eth_getCode at
latest through the client the scan used (no fallback; code or a failed check
refuses), and wipes every scalar in finally.

UI: Scan rows get "Payment details" (chain, address, ownership labelled apart
from receipt status, public/encrypted/raw downloads; raw behind a second
confirmation, never shown or copied); results get "Export all payment keys
(encrypted)" with count and chain shown first. Seller keys get "Master stealth
key backup (encrypted)" and "Open a stealth key export" (keypair list with
per-entry raw download behind a second confirmation; master keys load through
the hex-import path with a generated signing key and the unsaved-keys
confirmation). Panel close, chain switch, idle lock and key changes cancel.

Doc fix (18-stealth-keypair-export-formats.md section 7): the eth_getCode rule
did not say which exports it covers, which client is used, or what a refused
address does to an archive; it now names payment-key exports only, the scan's
client, and whole-archive refusal.

i18n: 92 new keys in en.json with machine-drafted es/ja/ar entries (the CI
catalog gate fails on missing keys), all classified in a new security group
stealthKeyExportUi so drafts are never shown.
